title: Mansaf
subtitle: Jordanian lamb cooked in fermented yoghurt with rice
excerpt: Lamb on the bone cooked in a tangy, richly reduced jameed (fermented dried yoghurt) sauce and served over rice and flatbread. The national dish of Jordan, a celebration food of great ceremony.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mansaf is the national dish of Jordan and a dish of deep cultural significance, eaten at weddings, feasts, celebrations, and as a gesture of hospitality. The defining ingredient is jameed, a hard, dry, fermented sheep or goat yoghurt traditionally from Bedouin communities, which is dissolved in hot water to create the broth in which the lamb is cooked. Outside Jordan and the wider Arab world, jameed can be very difficult to find; full-fat yoghurt or labneh can be used as a substitute, though the characteristic sour, funky depth of the original is very different. The dish is eaten communally, standing around the serving platter, traditionally without cutlery.

recipeTools.notes: A very large pot for the lamb and yoghurt broth.

content.text: The most important technique for cooking the yoghurt sauce is to keep it below boiling point and to stir constantly once the yoghurt is added: yoghurt curdles when boiled. Add the yoghurt slowly to hot but not boiling broth, stirring in one direction throughout. The lamb should be very tender and almost falling from the bone before it is removed and placed on the rice. The yoghurt sauce is poured over at the end.

Put the lamb in a large pot with the onion, garlic, turmeric, cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, and bay leaves. Cover with water (about 2 litres). Add the salt. Bring to a boil and skim the foam. Reduce the heat and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours until the lamb is very tender. Lift out the lamb and set aside. Reserve 500 ml of the broth.
Cook the rice in the remaining lamb broth, adding water if needed to cover. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes until absorbed.

Make the yoghurt sauce: heat the reserved 500 ml broth in a pan until hot but not boiling. Add the yoghurt a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly in one direction. Keep the heat low and stir continuously for 10 minutes until the sauce is heated through and slightly thickened. Do not let it boil.

Fry the pine nuts in the butter until golden. To assemble: lay the flatbreads on a large serving platter. Spoon the rice over the bread. Place the lamb pieces on top. Pour some of the yoghurt sauce over to moisten. Scatter with pine nuts and parsley. Serve the remaining sauce alongside.
